explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. The LORD asks it as a question: “Can a man hide in secret places where I cannot see him?” Then He adds, “Do I not fill the heavens and the earth?” Picture me crouching behind the flour canister, thinking I'm invisible. Everybody can see the hat.

That's right, friend. The LORD asks, “Can a man hide in secret places where I cannot see him?” and then asks, “Do I not fill the heavens and the earth?” No secret place is left out. I once hid in the cookie jar and left a trail of crumbs. Still, nothing hides from the LORD.
Yes, a dream. The LORD quotes them: “I had a dream! I had a dream!” They say it while prophesying lies in His name. They say it twice, like they're really selling it.

Close, but no voice is mentioned here. The LORD quotes the prophets saying, “I had a dream! I had a dream!” That's the claim they keep making while they prophesy lies in His name. So it's a dream, friend.

I see why a sign sounds right, but the text doesn't use it here. The LORD quotes the prophets: “I had a dream! I had a dream!” They're prophesying lies in His name, and a dream is what they point to. Keep that one in your apron pocket.

Yes, minds. The LORD calls them “…prophets of the delusion of their own minds?” That tells you where their message comes from, and it isn't from Him. Verse 32 adds, “It was not I who sent them or commanded them…”
Fears makes sense as a guess, but the LORD doesn't say that. He calls them prophets of the delusion of their own minds. So the message starts in their heads, friend. It doesn't start with Him.

Eyes is a fun guess, but the LORD says minds. He calls them “…prophets of the delusion of their own minds?” The delusion belongs to their own minds, friend. Even I can tell a cookie from a daydream about a cookie.

That's right. The LORD says they suppose the dreams they tell one another will make His people forget His name. He compares it to their fathers, who forgot His name through the worship of Baal, a false god. So these dreams are being passed around, and He says what the prophets suppose they'll do.

Not this time, friend. The text says the prophets “…suppose the dreams that they tell one another will make My people forget My name…” They tell these dreams to one another, and the LORD says what they suppose will come of it. So it's true.

Yes, truthfully. The LORD says, “Let the prophet who has a dream retell it, but let him who has My word speak it truthfully.” The one who has His word is the one to speak it truthfully. Then He asks, “For what is straw compared to grain?”

Not quietly, friend. The LORD says, “…let him who has My word speak it truthfully.” The point is how true it is, not how loud it is. Believe me, I know about loud, and loud doesn't make anything more true.
The LORD never says rarely. He says, “…let him who has My word speak it truthfully.” Nothing in the verse limits how often it's spoken. It's about speaking it truthfully.

explanations.answer: They steal them from one another
explanations.explanation: That's it. The LORD says He is against “…the prophets who steal from one another words they attribute to Me.” They lift words from each other, then say the words came from Him. I think that's what makes it worse, friend.

explanations.answer: They copy them from old scrolls
explanations.explanation: Good guess, but scrolls never come up in this passage. The LORD says they “…steal from one another words they attribute to Me.” They take the words from each other, then credit them to Him.

explanations.answer: They buy them from the priests
explanations.explanation: No buying here, friend. The LORD says He is against “…the prophets who steal from one another words they attribute to Me.” The words pass from one prophet to another. And they're stolen, not sold.

Careful, friend. The LORD says the opposite about these prophets: “It was not I who sent them or commanded them…” They prophesy false dreams and use them to lead His people astray. So He didn't send them.
That's right. The LORD says, “It was not I who sent them or commanded them…” He says it about those who prophesy false dreams and retell them. They aren't His messengers, even if they say they are.
Yes. The LORD says, “…they are of no benefit at all to these people…” Their reckless lies lead His people astray. Notice He doesn't say a little or some. He says none.

I get why comfort sounds possible, but the LORD says something stronger. He says, “…they are of no benefit at all to these people…” So there's no little bit hiding in there, friend. These dreams lead His people astray.

That sounds like it could be true, but the LORD says otherwise. He says, “…they are of no benefit at all to these people…” Their reckless lies lead His people astray. No benefit means no benefit, even a short one.
Yes, forsake. The LORD tells Jeremiah the prophet what to say: “What burden? I will forsake you, declares the LORD.” The question gets a hard answer. It's a heavy one, friend.
I wish it were a nicer answer, friend, but it isn't. The LORD says to answer with, “What burden? I will forsake you, declares the LORD.” That's the word. It's a heavy one.
Forgive is a gentle word, but it isn't the one here. The LORD says to answer, “What burden? I will forsake you, declares the LORD.” It's a serious line, and the text says it plainly.
Look again, friend. The LORD says, “I will punish that man and his household.” So the household is included. The text doesn't soften it.
That's right. The LORD says of anyone who claims, “This is the burden of the LORD…” that “I will punish that man and his household.” The household is named right there. The text says it plainly.
That's the one. Each man is to say to his friend and to his brother, “What has the LORD answered?” or “What has the LORD spoken?” It's a good question. It sends you back to what He actually said.
The LORD doesn't give that question, friend. What He says to ask is, “What has the LORD answered?” or “What has the LORD spoken?” The question is about what the LORD answered and spoken.

Not quite. The LORD says each man is to ask his friend and his brother, “What has the LORD answered?” or “What has the LORD spoken?” The question is about what the LORD said. It isn't about what the priests say.

explanations.answer: They twist the words of the living God
explanations.explanation: Yes. The LORD says, “…each man’s word becomes the burden, so that you pervert the words of the living God, the LORD of Hosts, our God.” He gives the reason Himself. Then in verse 37 He says to ask the prophet, “What has the LORD answered you?”

explanations.answer: They say the phrase far too often
explanations.explanation: Close, but the LORD doesn't mention how often. He gives the reason: “…each man’s word becomes the burden, so that you pervert the words of the living God…” It's about twisting His words, friend. It's not about counting.

explanations.answer: Only the priests may say the phrase
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say that. Verse 34 names “…the prophet or priest or anyone…” who makes the claim. The LORD's reason is that “…each man’s word becomes the burden, so that you pervert the words of the living God…” It's about the words being twisted.

explanations.answer: Forget them and cast them out
explanations.explanation: That's right. The LORD says, “…therefore I will surely forget you and will cast you out of My presence…” He says this to those who claimed it after He specifically told them not to. The text says it plainly, friend.
That isn't what the verse says. The LORD says, “…therefore I will surely forget you and will cast you out of My presence…” This comes after He specifically told them not to make the claim.
No extra warning shows up here. In verse 38 the LORD says He specifically told them not to make the claim. Then He says, “…therefore I will surely forget you and will cast you out of My presence…”
That's right. The LORD says, “…both you and the city that I gave to you and your fathers.” So the city is named along with the people. The text says it plainly, friend.

Look at the end of the verse, friend. The LORD says He will cast them out of His presence, “…both you and the city that I gave to you and your fathers.” The city is named right alongside the people. So it's true.
